en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the injustices of Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
The Supreme Court is the highest court in the Philippines and holds the judicial branch's power to interpret the Constitution.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of Luzon over 2,000 years ago using only hand tools.
Fe del Mundo was a pioneering Filipino pediatrician who invented an improvised bamboo incubator for premature babies lacking electricity.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white flower scientifically known as Jasminum sambac, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a distinctive two-step forward, one-step backward dance mimicking a river's current.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system where each character represents a syllable, written from left to right.
The Barong Tagalog is the traditional national attire for Filipino men, famously made from delicate pineapple fiber called piña.
Article III of the 1987 Philippine Constitution contains the Bill of Rights, which guarantees citizens' freedom of speech and religion.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his masterpiece Spoliarium.
